subject: MSA / Order Form: Evidence telemetry, pen-test window and security exhibit redlines
messages:
From: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@vitalityhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@vitalityhealth.com
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vitality MSA redlines — security exhibit / audit rights

Hi David and Laura,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the draft order form. We reviewed the MSA and attached a first-pass redline focused on the security exhibit and audit rights (see attached MSA_Vitality_redline_v1.docx). The main ask from our side: tighten the pen-test notice window and add clearer language on evidence delivery cadence for SOC 2 artifacts and incident logs. Two specific items: 

- Pen-test timing: we need a guaranteed 21-day notice for any active penetration tests that might affect our staging environment.
- Evidence telemetry: we need a list of the telemetry artifacts Redwood will provide post-SOC 2 (log exports, retention TTLs, scoped sample sets) and an expected delivery SLA for each artifact.

Can we get a short call tomorrow to align? If possible please include legal and whoever owns the security exhibit. Our preferred times: Thu 10–11am PT or Thu 2–3pm PT.

Thanks — attached redline includes inline comments for the evidence cadence.

Claire Hsu
Head of Security Programs
Vitality Health

Attachment: MSA_Vitality_redline_v1.docx (docx, 142KB)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@vitalityhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vitality MSA redlines — security exhibit / audit rights

Claire — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We're happy to align.

Quick plan from our side:
- Laura (sales/contracts) will own the procurement timeline and coordinate the order form.
- Marissa (legal ops) will triage redlines and produce a clean marked-up MSA for Vitality.
- Karthik (security/legal) will propose language for pen-test notice and the evidence artifact table.

Laura / Marissa / Karthik — can you prioritize a short 30-min sync tomorrow? Claire suggested 10–11am PT; we can do 10:15–10:45 PT.

Claire, attached in this reply we'll follow up with a proposed evidence cadence spreadsheet after our internal sync. In the meantime can you confirm whether the 21-day pen-test notice is negotiable to 14 days for non-production? Also, can you list the top 5 telemetry artifacts you need (examples: audit logs, API request traces, KV cache sampling, SOC 2 control evidence export, pen-test report summary)? That will help Karthik scope the redline.

Thanks,

—David
David Kim
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@vitalityhealth.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vitality MSA redlines — security exhibit / audit rights

Claire — appreciate the clear outline. We're booked for 10:15–10:45 PT tomorrow and will come prepared. A few quick notes ahead of the call so we can accelerate: 

1) Pen-test notice: 21 days is reasonable for production-impacting tests. For staging/non-prod we have an internal policy we try to adhere to of 14 days; our recommended compromise is 14 days for non-prod and 21 days for prod. We'll propose this in the redline.

2) Evidence cadence: rather than open-ended "deliver all SOC2 artifacts on request," we'd like to propose an evidence matrix with delivery SLAs (e.g., SOC 2 Type II report: within 3 business days of execution; audit logs export: within 5 business days; sampled-supporting artifacts: within 10 business days). We'll attach a prototype spreadsheet after the internal legal read.

3) Retention and telemetry: we cannot export full, always-on request traces at high frequency for all customers due to cost and privacy constraints. We can provide: aggregated request metrics, filtered request traces for requested time windows, audit logs (admin and API events), and a scoped set of KV-cache sampling logs (sanitized). We'll document retention TTLs for each artifact.

Marissa — do you want to confirm whether the proposed SLA buckets above are acceptable? Karthik — please prepare the exhibit redline bullets we discussed at last week's security sync (pen-test notice clause, scoped evidence table, SLA buckets, sampling/retention definitions).

Thanks,
Laura
VP, Customer Success (Contracts Lead)
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: security exhibit bullets for Vitality (see attached)

Team — attaching a short plaintext diff with the exhibit bullets: security-exhibit-diff.txt (attached). High-level summary: 

- Pen-test notice: 21 days for prod, 14 days for non-prod; Redwood will provide a staging/test environment notice window and a point-of-contact for scheduling and pre-test runbooks.
- Evidence matrix: defined artifacts and SLA buckets (SOC 2 Type II: 3 business days after signing NDA/acceptance; audit logs export: 5 business days; sampled artifacts: 10 business days). Artifacts listed: admin audit logs, API access logs (sanitized), system-level error logs, SOC 2 report, pen-test summary (redacted where required), KV cache sampling (anonymized IDs).
- Telemetry retention: standard artifact TTLs: logs retained 90 days hot, 365 days cold export; SOC artifacts retained per contract. Export formats: CSV/JSON for logs, PDF for reports.
- Scope/limits: explicit carveouts for data we cannot export (PII, full raw request bodies containing customer data) and an acceptance that some forensic activities will be performed via joint-incident response where we provide filtered datasets.

I flagged one legal question inline: should we tie the evidence SLAs to executed DFAs (data flow agreements) or to an order form acceptance? Marissa / Neha — recommend we choose one canonical trigger to avoid downstream disputes.

I'll be on the call at 10:15 PT and can walk through the diff.

—Karthik
Sr. Counsel, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: security-exhibit-diff.txt (txt, 9KB)

From: Tom Baker <tbaker@vitalityhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@vitalityhealth.com>, procurement@vitalityhealth.com
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vitality MSA redlines — security exhibit / audit rights

Thanks everyone for the quick responses and the proposed approach. Confirming the 10:15–10:45 PT slot — Claire will join with procurement and our legal counsel for the call. A couple of quick asks before we sync so the call stays focused: 

- Please bring the evidence-cadence-proposal.xlsx with the SLA buckets mapped to artifact examples and sample delivery mechanics (SFTP/secure Drive links/DocuSign attestation).
- Can Karthik briefly outline the carveouts you mentioned and the proposed trigger for SLA (we prefer the trigger to be the executed order form if possible).
- For pen-test notices: Vitality's security team wants explicit confirmation that any tests involving active exploit attempts to non-prod environments will be coordinated through a dedicated war-room and that Redwood will share a pre-test runbook 48 hours before execution.

If you can drop the spreadsheet to the Drive link in the hubspot thread before 10:15 that would be ideal. Looking forward to the call.

Tom Baker
Sr. Manager, Procurement
Vitality Health

Attachment referenced: evidence-cadence-proposal.xlsx (we'll expect this on the Drive)
